extracted.intended_audience: Inpatient Rehabilitation Facility (IRF) administrators, Medicare payment policy staff, and stakeholders commenting on IRF PPS rules
extracted.subtask_description: Final rule guidance and methodological standards for FY2025 Inpatient Rehabilitation Facility Prospective Payment System (IRF PPS), including wage index adoption, budget-neutrality calculations, outlier methodology, CCR ceilings, and IRF Quality Reporting Program requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption of OMB CBSA delineations for FY 2025
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt the revised OMB CBSA delineations contained in OMB Bulletin No. 23-01 for purposes of the FY 2025 wage index updates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS believes using the latest available labor market area delineations is important to maintain an accurate and up-to-date payment system reflecting population shifts and labor market conditions and to increase the integrity of the IRF PPS wage index system. CMS will not modify OMB delineations using additional data (e.g., for individual areas or IRFs) because doing so would increase administrative burden and complexity, and because delineation changes are applied budget-neutrally under the wage index. CMS interprets the MAPS Act as permitting adoption with explanation rather than automatic application and states its proposed rule meets MAPS Act requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition policy for FY 2024 rural IRFs reclassified as urban in FY 2025
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement a budget-neutral three-year phase-out of the rural adjustment for existing FY 2024 rural IRFs that will become urban in FY 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This transition policy is intended to alleviate payment impacts for IRFs that lose the FY 2024 rural payment adjustment or experience payment reductions solely because of redesignation. CMS will not implement a transition policy for urban facilities that become rural in FY 2025 because those IRFs will receive the full rural adjustment of 14.9% beginning October 1, 2024. CMS decided not to phase in revised CBSAs over 3 years overall, finding such an approach overly complex to administer, but will apply a 3-year phase-out specifically for the rural adjustment loss for affected FY 2024 rural IRFs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permanent 5-percent cap policy on wage index decreases
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain an existing permanent 5-percent cap policy that limits decreases in an IRF's wage index value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS views the permanent 5-percent cap as substantially mitigating financial impacts of updated CBSA delineations. The cap is applied in the wage index calculations and is considered alongside any transition policies. Comments requested uncapped application; CMS states the cap should be applied budget-neutrally and in accordance with statutory budget neutrality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget-neutral requirement for wage index adjustments (statutory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjustments or updates to the IRF wage index under section 1886(j)(6) of the Act must be made in a budget-neutral manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS references statutory requirement and prior rulemaking; commenters suggesting non-budget-neutral application of caps were rejected. The budget-neutral wage adjustment factor is computed per the steps codified and applied to the standard payment conversion factor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology to calculate FY 2025 budget-neutral wage adjustment factor
rubrics_metrics.description: Four-step methodology to compute the budget-neutral wage adjustment factor (resulting in FY 2025 factor 0.9924).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Step 1: Calculate total estimated IRF PPS payments using FY 2024 labor-related share and FY 2024 wage indexes. Step 2: Calculate total estimated IRF PPS payments using FY 2025 wage index values and FY 2025 labor-related share (74.4%). Step 3: Divide Step 1 amount by Step 2 amount to obtain budget-neutral wage adjustment factor (0.9924). Step 4: Apply the factor to the FY 2025 IRF PPS standard payment amount after increase factor application to determine the FY 2025 standard payment conversion factor. Methodology follows FY 2004 IRF PPS final rule and §412.624(e)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation and application of labor-related share
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine labor-related portion of the standard payment amount by multiplying the unadjusted Federal payment rate by the FY 2025 labor-related share (74.4%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The labor-related share is based on the 2021-based IRF market basket relative importance (74.4%). To compute non-labor portion, subtract labor portion from unadjusted prospective payment. The labor portion is then multiplied by the applicable IRF wage index from the wage index tables to compute the wage-adjusted labor amount.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard payment conversion factor calculation procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Process to compute the FY 2025 standard payment conversion factor starting from FY 2024 factor and applying market basket increase, budget-neutrality, and CMG relative weights adjustments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin with FY 2024 standard payment conversion factor ($18,541). Apply market basket increase factor for FY 2025 (×1.030 after productivity adjustment). Multiply by budget-neutrality factor for wage index updates (×0.9924) and by budget-neutrality factor for CMG relative weights (×0.9976) to yield FY 2025 standard payment conversion factor ($18,907). Table 10 documents the calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology for adjusting prospective payment rates (calculation steps)
rubrics_metrics.description: Stepwise method to convert unadjusted CMG prospective payments into wage-adjusted and facility-adjusted final payments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 1) Multiply unadjusted prospective payment by labor-related share to get labor portion. 2) Multiply labor portion by wage index to obtain wage-adjusted labor amount. 3) Add wage-adjusted labor amount to non-labor portion to get wage-adjusted Federal payment. 4) Multiply wage-adjusted payment by appropriate rural and LIP adjustments (if applicable). 5) Compute teaching status additional payment by multiplying teaching status adjustment by the wage-and-rural-adjusted amount; add to produce final adjusted payment. Example provided comparing Facility A (rural) and Facility B (urban).

rubrics_metrics.name: Outlier payment eligibility and calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: A case qualifies for an outlier payment if the estimated cost of the case exceeds the adjusted outlier threshold; outlier payment equals 80% of the difference between estimated cost and threshold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimated cost of a case = IRF's overall Cost-to-Charge Ratio (CCR) × Medicare allowable covered charge. Adjusted outlier threshold = CMG payment adjusted by relevant facility-level adjustments + adjusted threshold amount (also facility-adjusted). Policy authority: section 1886(j)(4) of the Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outlier threshold target of 3 percent of total estimated payments
rubrics_metrics.description: Set the outlier threshold so that estimated outlier payments equal approximately 3 percent of total estimated IRF PPS payments under simulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methodology: simulate aggregate payments and iteratively adjust threshold until outlier payments equal 3% of total payments. CMS has used this 3% target since FY 2002 to balance reducing financial risk for high-cost patients and preserving adequate payments for non-outlier cases. For FY 2025 CMS proposed and finalized a threshold (updated to $12,043) using FY 2023 claims and most recent available data and accounting for budget-neutrality adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of most recent full fiscal year data to set rates and thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the most recent full fiscal year of data (e.g., FY 2023 claims, FY 2022 cost reports) as the best overall predictor of upcoming fiscal year experience to update prospective payment rates and determine outlier threshold and CCRs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS will update data between proposed and final rules to incorporate more complete claims or cost report data. Commenter suggestions to use rolling averages (e.g., 3-year) were considered but not adopted because they may not maintain the 3% outlier pool objective or would reduce predictability of meeting the 3% target.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response to suggested modifications to outlier methodology (stability measures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of suggestions such as 3-year rolling average, outlier reconciliation policy, establishing baseline and indexing, capping IRF outlier receipts, or reducing the outlier pool.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS appreciates suggestions but declines to adopt a 3-year rolling average because it would not necessarily maintain outlier payments at the 3% target and prefers using the most recent full fiscal year of data. Any future adjustments (e.g., reconciliation policy or limits) would require careful assessment of impacts on access and integrity of the 3% outlier pool.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analysis of concentration and targeting of outlier payments
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider and analyze commenter concerns that outlier payments may be concentrated among a small subset of providers or driven by inefficient cost structures rather than patient complexity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS will examine the distribution and targeting of outlier payments and consider additional analysis; any policy changes to limit outlier payments or adjust thresholds must assess effects on access for high-cost populations and preserve the outlier pool integrity at 3%.

rubrics_metrics.name: IRF Cost-to-Charge Ratio (CCR) national averages and ceiling methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate national average CCRs separately for rural and urban IRFs and set a national CCR ceiling at mean plus three standard deviations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For FY 2025 CMS proposed and finalized national average rural CCR (0.485 proposal; finalized 0.485 reported in analysis, final stated 0.485 earlier) and urban CCR (proposed 0.492 but finalized 0.405 using FY 2022 data), and a national CCR ceiling computed as national average CCR + 3×standard deviation, resulting in a final ceiling of 1.50 for FY 2025. Averages are weighted by IRFs' estimated costs; use most recently submitted cost reports (FY 2022) and do not use cost report data prior to FY 2004.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of CCR national averages and ceiling
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply national urban/rural CCRs and the national CCR ceiling in specified situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply national averages to: new IRFs without a first MCR, IRFs with an overall CCR exceeding the national CCR ceiling (replace their CCR with appropriate national average), and IRFs lacking accurate data to calculate an overall CCR. If an IRF's CCR exceeds the ceiling for FY 2025, replace it with the national average CCR appropriate to its urban/rural location.

rubrics_metrics.name: IRF Quality Reporting Program (IRF QRP) statutory reporting requirement and penalty
rubrics_metrics.description: IRFs must submit standardized patient assessment data in accordance with the IRF QRP requirements; failure to submit results in a 2 percentage-point reduction in the annual increase factor for discharges during the FY.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authority: section 1886(j)(7) of the Act; program requirements codified at §412.634. The IRF QRP applies to freestanding IRFs and inpatient rehabilitation units of hospitals or CAHs paid under IRF PPS.

rubrics_metrics.name: General considerations for selection and removal of IRF QRP measures
rubrics_metrics.description: IRF QRP measure selection and removal follow considerations discussed in FY 2016 IRF PPS final rule and §412.634(b)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS refers readers to the FY 2016 final rule for a detailed discussion of considerations used for selection of IRF QRP quality, resource use, or other measures. Measures may be evaluated for removal based on the factors outlined in the regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of adopted IRF QRP measures (18 measures)
rubrics_metrics.description: IRF QRP currently has 18 adopted measures including assessment-based measures, NHSN infection measures, staff vaccination measures, and claims-based measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 13 lists the 18 adopted measures and their data sources, including: Pressure Ulcer/Injury; Application of Falls; Discharge Mobility Score; Discharge Self-Care Score; Drug Regimen Review with Follow-Up; Transfer of Health Information to Provider/Patient; Discharge Function Score; COVID-19 Vaccine (patients); NHSN CAUTI; NHSN CDI; HCP Influenza Vaccine; HCP COVID-19 Vaccine; Medicare Spending Per Beneficiary (MSPB) - PAC; Discharge to Community; Potentially Preventable 30-Day Post-Discharge Readmission; Potentially Preventable Within Stay Readmission. CMS did not propose new measures for this rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed collection of new standardized patient assessment data elements (SDOH) for FY 2028 IRF QRP
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose requiring IRFs to report four new items as standardized patient assessment data elements under social determinants of health (SDOH): one Living Situation item, two Food items, and one Utilities item; also propose modification of the Transportation item.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These would be added to the IRF-PAI; section 1899B(b)(1) requires PAC providers to submit standardized patient assessment data with respect to admission and discharge and as Secretary deems appropriate. The proposal describes timing (beginning with FY 2028 IRF QRP) and cross-references more detailed descriptions in the proposed rule sections. Definitions and statutory references for standardized patient assessment data are provided.
